description:
The Rust test suites prove many properties several times over, at layers above their owners, through fixtures that each test file re-implements. This epic gives each property one owning test on shared fixtures and shared interface contracts, so the suite is cheaper to run and a failure names one cause.

## Background

Duplicated properties, verified at `79c177fbd`:

- Exit codes. `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs` (32 tests) binds every projected command row in both invocation forms and checks completeness (`test_command_exit_codes_every_row_is_verified`, `:1128`). `exit_code_tests.rs` (39 subprocess tests, 1,637 lines) re-proves the same codes, for example success (`:36` vs `:774`), cycle (`:69` vs `:818`) and unconfirmed delete (`:1566` vs `:966`). `invocation_exit_status_parity_tests.rs` re-proves the human/machine parity the both-forms helper already asserts.
- Query semantics. `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/domain_queries_tests.rs` owns the pure query filters. `crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/query_tests.rs` re-proves them in 25 subprocess tests (1,422 lines), each spawning `jit init` and several `issue create` processes. `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/harness_demo.rs` (526 lines, 14 tests), self-described as a "Demonstration of test harness usage", re-proves queries, blocking, cycle rejection and gates. `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/workflow_tests.rs:529-743` re-proves dependency auto-transitions owned by `crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:2427`.
- Cycle detection. Four tests in `crates/jit/src/commands/batch_create.rs:686-711` repeat `crates/jit/src/graph/keyed.rs` tests over a 10-line adapter. `harness_demo.rs:133`, `cli_repo_workflow/integration_test.rs:616` and `exit_code_tests.rs:69` re-prove dependency cycle rejection owned by `crates/jit/src/graph/mod.rs`.
- Mutation finalization. About 800 lines of `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs` (`:1735-2555`) re-prove `repository_state` finalization.
- List envelope. `count == len` is asserted per command by 19 subprocess tests in `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/list_envelope_tests.rs`, again by `cli_query_graph/search_tests.rs:236`, `cli_repo_workflow/artifact_conformance_cli_tests.rs:647` and `cli_repo_workflow/profile_cli_tests.rs:1940`.

Fixtures and contracts:

- No shared subprocess fixture exists. `fn jit_binary` is defined in 56 files. 42 files spawn through `assert_cmd`'s `cargo_bin!` and 68 through `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit")`. 57 files define a local `setup_test_repo` or `setup_repo`. 112 `split_whitespace` sites scrape ids from human-readable output. 17 files hand-roll `git init`. No file removes inherited `JIT_*` variables, so a developer's agent identity leaks into spawned processes.
- In-process fixtures have parallel copies: `fixture_issue` 5 times, `TaxonomyRepo` twice, `memory_executor` twice with different config and index seeding. Fixture code lives in `crate::test_utils`, `crate::commands::test_helpers`, `crate::test_taxonomy`, `crates/jit/tests/common/harness.rs` and suite `main.rs` files.
- The shipped item-kind declarations are hand-copied: `CANONICAL_ITEM_KINDS` in `crates/jit/tests/common/harness.rs:59-100` restates `profiles/jit-default/manifest.toml`, and the `D-[0-9]+` id pattern appears 14 times.
- `IssueStore` has two implementations (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1045`, `crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs:820`) and no shared conformance suite. A cross-backend matrix exists only for `RepositoryStateStore` (`repository_state_store_tests.rs:660`). `InMemoryStorage::read_path_bytes` reads the real disk and ignores `at_commit` (`memory.rs:987-1022`).
- Process-wide state. `CurrentDirGuard` serialises working-directory changes. Environment changes in `crates/jit/src/config.rs` (14 calls), `crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs` and `crates/server/src/lib.rs` run without a shared guard; the restoring helper `EnvironmentRestore` is private to `test_utils`' own tests (`crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs:1308`).
- Missing toolchains pass. `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/merged_tree_gate_verification_tests.rs:47-53` prints `SKIP:` and passes when `scripts/cargo-ci-selftest.sh` (622 lines) exits 2 for missing git, cargo or jq. That script runs nested cargo builds of six fixture crates inside the default suite. `build_profile_policy_tests.rs:332` runs `scripts/profile-test-suite.sh --self-test` the same way.
- Fixture cache. `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs:78-860` keys a profiled-repository cache on SHA-256 hashes of the test and `jit` executables, adds a nextest receipt path (`:336-470`) to skip that hashing, compiles a hidden `__test-fixture-setup` subcommand into the product binary (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:2357`), and lists test names by regex in `.config/nextest.toml`. The audit measured the debug `jit` binary at 141 MB, hashing at about 0.24 s wall, and building a profiled repository at about 0.13 s.

Build footprint against `@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint` (`scripts/rust-build-budget.sh`): 10 integration-test targets against a limit of 12; the last recorded active test-executable total is 1.62 GiB across 14 executables against a 2 GiB limit (`dev/benchmarks/rust-build-budgets/README.md`). Each suite executable on disk is 83-136 MB because each links the whole `jit` library.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Command-to-exit-code bindings and their human/machine parity are proven only by the exit-code projection suite. Other subprocess tests assert only what they add, such as remediation text or empty stdout on error.
- [hard] REQ-02: Query filters, dependency auto-transitions and cycle detection are proven only at the domain and graph layers. CLI and harness tests of those commands assert one wiring case per subcommand or flag, and the harness demonstration suite is deleted, its unique cases moved beside their owners.
- [hard] REQ-03: Mutation finalization is proven once, in the repository-state layer. Storage tests cover only the backend behaviour storage adds.
- [hard] REQ-04: The list-envelope `count` property is proven by one test that covers every list-emitting command, and no per-command test re-asserts it.
- [hard] REQ-05: One shared subprocess fixture spawns `jit` for every CLI test. It owns its temporary repository, uses one spawn convention, removes inherited `JIT_*` variables, initialises git on request, and reads created ids from machine-readable output. No test file defines its own binary locator, repository setup or id scraping from human-readable output.
- [hard] REQ-06: Issue construction, the taxonomy repository and the memory executor each have one definition in shared test support. The memory executor seeds configuration and index through the product's own initialisation, with no literal schema version.
- [hard] REQ-07: Tests that need the shipped item kinds derive them from the shipped default package. A deliberately custom kind is a minimal literal that says it is custom.
- [hard] REQ-08: Every `IssueStore` implementation runs one shared reader and writer conformance suite. The in-memory backend's path reads, decoding and commit-pinned reads pass it, and implementation-specific tests cover only implementation-specific behaviour.
- [hard] REQ-09: Tests reach the working directory and environment variables only through shared scoped guards that serialise and restore them. Every test passes alone, in any order and in parallel.
- [hard] REQ-10: A test whose tool is missing fails. The default test suite runs no nested cargo build; shell-script self-tests run as declared gates over the scripts.
- [hard] REQ-11: The profiled-repository fixture is reused under a key derived only from its inputs (package bytes and crate source). The product binary has no hidden fixture subcommand, and no test-runner configuration lists individual test names.
- [hard] REQ-12: The build-footprint budget checker passes. Integration-target count and active test-executable bytes are measured before and after the change and reported.

## Notes

Serves `@/inv/orthogonal-tests` (one owning test per property, at the cheapest layer), `@/inv/shared-test-contracts` (shared fixtures; every implementation runs one contract), `@/inv/no-ignored-tests` (a skipped test is a held-out test), `@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint`, and `@/charter/D-18` (delete re-proofs and private fixture copies rather than maintain them). Script self-tests become repository gates per `@/charter/D-2`.

Deleting a re-proof keeps the owning test; coverage moves, it is not lost. Where an owner lacks a case a deleted test covered, the case moves to the owner.
title: Give each test property one owning test on shared fixtures and contracts
